intended_object: The restriction-of-scalars functor from finitely generated projective S-modules to finitely generated projective R-modules along a ring map φ : R → S, defined when S, viewed as an R-module through φ, is finitely generated projective. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the name.
explanation:
The definition takes Mathlib's `ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ`, precomposes it with the inclusion of the full subcategory of finite projective S-modules, and lifts the result into the full subcategory of finite projective R-modules. The lift is justified by `finiteProjective_restrictScalars`, which uses transitivity of finiteness and of projectivity.

The hypothesis `hC` (S is finite projective over R through φ) is exactly what is needed. It is sufficient, and it is also necessary, because S is itself a finite projective S-module. So it is neither stronger nor weaker than the functor requires.

The setting is general enough: arbitrary (possibly noncommutative) rings with left modules, and independent universes for the scalars and the carriers. `FiniteProjective R` is the full subcategory of `ModuleCat R` cut out by `Module.Finite ∧ Module.Projective`, which is the standard notion.

Mathlib provides the general functor on all modules (`ModuleCat.restrictScalars`) but has no version restricted to finite projective modules. This definition is the standard construction, obtained by lifting the general functor rather than rewriting it.
